cards.title: 3.1.1 The Concept of Force
body: A spring balance, a 1 kg mass, a length of spring and a small box.
In physics, a force is a push or a pull exerted by one object on another.
When the wind blows the leaves of a tree, the wind exerts a force.
Forces are physical quantities that can be measured. using a force meter.

cards.title: 3.1.2 Newton’s First Law of Motion
body: When no forces are exerted on an object or when the vector sum of all the forces is zero, the net force is zero.
If an object moves with a constant velocity, then the net force on the object is zero.
The forward force must be equal in size and opposite in direction to the force of friction in order to maintain constant velocity.
If there is no friction, there is no need for a forward force.

cards.title: 3.1.3 Newton’s Second Law of Motion
body: Newton’s first law describes what happens when the net force acting on an object is zero.
In that case, the object either remains at rest or continues to move in a straight line at constant speed.
In other words, an unbalanced force, or net force, accelerates or decelerates.
Newton’s second law involves force, mass, and acceleration.

cards.title: 3.1.4 Newton’s Third Law of Motion
body: Newton’s first and second laws explain how the changes in the motion of a single object changes.
Newton stated that a force applied to one object always comes from another object.
For example, the force of gravity on a falling orange comes from the Earth and the magnetic force acting on a metal nail comes from a magnet.
In other words, one force cannot exist without the other.

cards.title: 3.1.5 Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation
body: One day Sir Isaac Newton was sitting in his garden and noticed an apple dropped from a tree.
The sight of the falling apple made him think about the problem of motion of the planets.
Newton realised that the force on the apple must be proportional to its mass.
Gravitational force is a property of all matter; that is, every object attracts every other object with a gravitational force.

cards.title: 3.1.6 Normal Force
body: The cupboard exerts a downward force on the floor.
According to Newton’s third law of motion, the floor exerts an upward force on the cupboard.
The force that is exerted by a supporting surface on an object that is resting (standing, sitting, lying) on it is called the normal force, FN.
Normal force is a contact force between two solid objects and acts that is perpendicularly to the contact surfaces (e.g. cupboard and floor).

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Which of the following is the standard SI unit of force?

steps.text: **Given:** Basic units of physical quantities.
**Formula:** The SI unit of force is the Newton ($$\text{N}$$, named after Sir Isaac Newton).
**Substitution:** Comparing options: Joule is for energy, Kilogram is for mass, Watt is for power, and Newton is for force.
**Final Result:** The correct option is **D. Newton**.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: An object is acted upon by two collinear forces: $$12\text{ N}$$ acting East and $$8\text{ N}$$ acting West. What is the net force acting on the object?

steps.text: **Given:** Force East $$F_1 = +12\text{ N}$$, Force West $$F_2 = -8\text{ N}$$.
**Formula:** $$F_{net} = F_1 + F_2$$
**Substitution:** $$F_{net} = +12\text{ N} + (-8\text{ N}) = +4\text{ N}$$ (which points East).
**Final Result:** The net force is **$$4\text{ N}$$ East**.

**Given:** Force East $$F_1 = +12\text{ N}$$, Force West $$F_2 = -8\text{ N}$$.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If the net unbalanced force acting on an object is zero, according to Newton's first law, the object must:

options.C: Maintain its constant velocity (or remain at rest)

cards.why:
**Given:** Net force $$F_{net} = 0$$.

**Formula:** From Newton's first law, if $$F_{net} = 0$$, then acceleration $$a = 0$$.

**Substitution:** Zero acceleration means the velocity of the object does not change over time. Thus, it remains at rest if initially at rest, or continues at a constant velocity.

**Final Result:** The correct option is **C. Maintain its constant velocity (or remain at rest)**.

cards.title: 3.2.1 Friction
body: A ball rolling along the ground gradually slows down and finally comes to rest.
A car also comes to rest once its engine is switched off.
In all these situations no force appears to be acting on the objects, yet their speed gradually decreases and they come to rest after some time.
The force responsible for changing the state of motion of objects is the force of friction.

cards.title: 3.2.2 Advantages and Disadvantages of Friction
body: Car tyres are rough, so they provide high friction and prevent the car from sliding on the road.
A matchstick is lit because of friction.
When a machine is operated, there is friction between moving parts, which causes the parts to wear down and wastes energy.

cards.title: 3.2.3 Methods of Reducing Friction
body: When surfaces are highly polished, there are fewer irregularities and friction decreases.
When oil, grease or graphite is applied between the moving parts of a machine, it forms a thin layer which prevents the moving surfaces from directly rubbing against each other (Fig. 3.40).
The oil reduces the interlocking of irregularities and movement becomes smooth.
The substances which decrease friction are called lubricants.

cards.title: 3.2.4 Types of Friction
body: The amount of friction that exists between two bodies depends on the state of each of the bodies, that is whether they are at rest, sliding or rolling.
Depending upon these different states, friction can be classified into three types.
The frictional force present between two bodies in contact when there is no relative motion between them is called static friction, fs.
The force of gravity mg is cancelled by the normal reaction force, FN, of the table.

cards.title: 3.2.5 The Laws of Friction
body: Friction experiments indicate that there are certain factors that affect friction.
The magnitude of the friction force depends on the force pressing the two surfaces together and on the nature of the surfaces.
The coefficient of friction is a unit less quantity.
The larger the value of the coefficient of friction, the larger is the friction present between two surfaces.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following physical quantities is the quantitative measure of a body's inertia?
cards.why:
**Given:** Inertia of a body.

**Formula:** Mass is defined as the quantitative measure of a body's inertia. The larger the mass, the more the body resists changes to its state of motion.

**Substitution:** While weight changes with gravity, mass is constant and directly measures the body's resistance to acceleration.

**Final Result:** The correct option is **D. Mass**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, according to Newton's law of universal gravitation, the gravitational force between them:
cards.why:
**Given:** Initial distance $$r$$, final distance $$r' = 2r$$.

**Formula:** $$F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$$

**Substitution:** $$F' = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{(2r)^2} = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{4r^2} = \frac{1}{4}F$$.

**Final Result:** The gravitational force becomes **one-fourth** of the original force.

glossary.meaning: Extension is the increase in length from the normal, unstretched length of the spring; compression is the decrease from its normal length.
Force is defined as a push or a pull on an object.
Elastic limit is the limit to the applied force from which the material will recover when the force is removed.
Inertia is a property of matter that is constant everywhere in the universe.
Mass is a measure of an object’s inertia.
Apparent weight is the force an object experiences as a result of all the forces which act on it to give the object acceleration.
Gravitational force is a property of all matter; that is, every object attracts every other object with a gravitational force.
Normal force is a contact force between two solid objects and acts that is perpendicularly to the contact surfaces (e.g. cupboard and floor).
Friction is defined as the force which opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
Momentum is a vector quantity and its SI unit is kg.m/s.
Impulse is a vector quantity and its SI unit is N.s or kg.m/s.

tips.text: Force is defined as a push or a pull on an object. It is a vector quantity and its SI unit is the newton (N).
Net force, resultant force or unbalanced force is the vector sum of all the forces acting on an object at the same time.
A force exerted on an object may change the shape and size of the object, change the velocity of the object, or change the direction of motion of the object.
Elastic materials are materials that recover their original shape and size when the force is removed after they are stretched, compressed, bent or twisted.
Inelastic materials are materials that do not return to their original shape when the force is removed.
Elastic limit is the limit to the applied force from which the material will recover when the force is removed.

The Italian Galileo Galilei (1564 - 1642) was one of the first scientists to understand that a force doesn’t need to be continually applied to an object to keep it moving. He claimed that no resultant force is required to maintain uniform motion.
Galileo explained that a force is needed to keep an object moving on a level surface because the force of friction opposes the motion.
Without friction, an object will never stop moving.
To prove this statement, Galileo conducted an experiment using two inclined planes set end-to-end, one tilted down and the other up. He rolled a ball down the first incline.

similar.q: Newton's third law refers to "action-reaction forces". These forces always occur in pairs and  A) sometimes act on the same object.  B) always act on the same object.  C) may be at right angles.  D) never act on the same object.  E) always act at right angles.
similar.a: D. never act on the same object. — Action and reaction are equal in size, opposite in direction, along the same line, and act on DIFFERENT bodies (G9 p.157–160) – that is why they never cancel each other. Answer: D.

similar.q:
A force of 5 N acts on a body of weight 10 N. The acceleration of the body, in m/s², is
[g = 10 m/s²]  A) 50.  B) 5.  C) 0.5.  D) 2.  E) 20.
similar.a: B. 5. — Newton's second law: a = F/m = 5 N ÷ 1 kg = 5 m/s² (G9 p.139–150). Answer: B. (C, 0.5, wrongly divides by the weight.)
